transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?
Lately I keep thinking my family might be better off without me, and those thoughts are starting to scare me. I've just been feeling so heavy, and I didn't know where else to turn.
How long have you been experiencing these heavy feelings and thoughts about your family being better off without you?

This deep, hopeless feeling and those dark thoughts have been going on steadily for about six months now, starting even a little before my work contracts officially ended. I’ve had these swings between highs and lows for several years, but this current stretch is by far the worst it's ever been.
Have you had any periods in the past six months where your mood significantly improved for at least a couple of weeks, or has it been consistently low?

For these past six months, it has been consistently low and heavy every single day without any real relief. But right before this long crash started, I went through a stretch where I felt the exact opposite—unusually up, wired, and just full of energy.

Can you tell me more about that period before this current low stretch when you felt unusually up and full of energy, how long did it last and what were some of the things you did or experienced during that time?

That stretch lasted for a few weeks where I was so wired I barely slept, often staying up until 3 AM sketching designs and convinced I'd make my workshop a famous online brand. I got really snappy with my wife if she questioned my plans, and I was so distracted that I started a dozen different projects but couldn't actually finish any of them.
Can you estimate how many of these high and low mood swings you've experienced in the past year, and did any of them last for more than two weeks at a time?

This past year has really just been dominated by this one major cycle—that high, wired spell that lasted for a few weeks, followed by this heavy low that has been dragging on for six months now. While these swings have come and gone for several years, this past year has mostly been this one long, painful stretch since my business troubles started.
Have you experienced any other episodes similar to the few weeks of feeling 'unusually up and full of energy' in the past, or was that a one-time occurrence before this current six-month low period?

No, it wasn't a one-time thing; these swings between feeling highly revved up with big plans and then crashing into deep lows have actually been coming and going for several years. It's just that this current low stretch is by far the most severe and hopeless I've ever felt.
Can you describe how often these high and low episodes occurred before this past year, and did they follow a pattern or seem to be triggered by specific events?

In the past, those swings would come and go every few years without much of a pattern, and they were never nearly as bad as this. But this current, severe crash was definitely triggered when my two big commercial contracts suddenly ended and my apprentice moved to the mainland, forcing a transition I wasn't ready for.

Can you clarify if the duration of your high episodes has been consistently short, lasting only a few weeks, while the low episodes have varied in length, with this current one being the longest at six months?

Yes, that's exactly right. Those high periods of intense energy and big planning usually only last for a few weeks at a time before fading away. The low periods have always been much longer and vary in length, but this current one is definitely the longest and most severe, dragging on steadily for about six months now.

Have you ever had a period where you switched directly from a high episode to a low episode without a significant period of normal mood in between, or have you typically had some time with a more stable mood between these episodes?

For this recent episode, the transition was very direct—I went straight from being highly energized and making big plans right into this heavy, dark crash. In the past, I usually had some stable, normal periods in between my swings, but this time the drop-off was sudden and severe.

During your current low period, have you experienced any symptoms that are typically associated with your high episodes, such as increased energy or reduced need for sleep, even if they are not as severe as during your high episodes?

No, I haven't had any of that high energy or lack of sleep during this low period. In fact, it has been the complete opposite—I feel constantly drained, exhausted, and like I'm moving through mud. It is nothing like the wired, sleepless feeling I had before I crashed.
Have you experienced at least two years of symptoms with both major depressive episodes and hypomanic episodes, but no full manic episodes, to help clarify the pattern of your mood swings?

Yes, these swings between feeling overly revved up and crashing into heavy lows have been coming and going for several years, well over the two-year mark. While those high periods were intense and full of non-stop energy, I never completely lost control or needed to be hospitalized, and they always just ended in a crash back into depression.
Have you ever experienced a high episode that lasted long enough or was severe enough to cause significant impairment in your social or occupational functioning, or required hospitalization?

No, I’ve never been hospitalized, and during those high times I didn't feel like they were ruining my life because I just felt like I had endless energy and big plans, even though I was irritable and left projects unfinished. The real trouble keeping up with my work, falling behind on bills, and pulling away from my friends only hit me when I crashed into this current low phase.
During your high episodes, did you ever experience any psychotic symptoms, such as hallucinations or delusions, or did you ever have to be removed from a situation due to risky behavior?

No, I’ve never experienced anything like that—I never heard voices, had delusions, or had to be removed or hospitalized because of my behavior. Even though I was extremely energized, stayed up all night, and had grand plans, I never lost touch with reality or got into that kind of trouble.
Can you confirm whether your high episodes have always been brief, typically lasting only a few weeks, and never severe enough to cause significant problems in your daily life or relationships?

Yes, that's correct—those high times have always been brief, usually lasting just a few weeks. While I did get snappy and irritated with my wife and kids when they questioned my unrealistic plans, it didn't cause major disruptions at the time. The severe trouble, like falling behind on bills, missing work deadlines, and completely pulling away from my friends, only started once I crashed into this current low.

Have you ever had a high episode that, while not reaching the level of a full manic episode, caused enough problems in your daily life or relationships that it significantly impacted your functioning or required intervention from others?

Right before this crash, I had a spell where I was unusually wired, staying up until 2 or 3 AM with grand plans for the shop. It caused real strain because I got very snappy and irritated with my wife and kids when they tried to get me to slow down or pointed out that the numbers didn't make financial sense. I was also so distracted that I started a dozen different projects but left them all unfinished, which frustrated everyone.

Did any of your high episodes, although brief, cause significant distress or impairment in social or occupational functioning, or required intervention from others to prevent harm to yourself or others?

No, those high periods never got so bad that I needed emergency intervention or became a danger to myself or others, even if I was irritable and disorganized. Nobody ever had to step in to keep me safe. It is really this current low state where I am feeling the most severe impairment and distress.
Did you experience any significant impairment in social or occupational functioning during your high episodes that was noticeable to others, even if you didn't require hospitalization?

Yes, even though I didn't need a hospital, my behavior during those high times was definitely noticeable and caused real problems. I would get very snappy and irritated with my family if they questioned my plans, and my work suffered because I was constantly pacing around and starting multiple projects without actually finishing the orders I already had.

Can you confirm if any of your past hypomanic episodes, although brief, involved symptoms that were severe enough to cause noticeable problems in your daily life or relationships, but not to the extent of requiring hospitalization or causing significant impairment?

Yes, those up phases definitely caused noticeable tension in my daily routine and relationships, especially when I'd stay up until 3 AM and get very snappy with my family for questioning my plans. I would also leave multiple projects scattered and unfinished, which made the workshop a mess. But while it caused real strain, it never led to hospitalization or any kind of complete, catastrophic breakdown.
Did any of your high episodes, even though brief, involve psychotic symptoms or require hospitalization due to severity, which could help differentiate between the current diagnostic considerations?

No, I don't recall ever being hospitalized or experiencing extreme symptoms like losing touch with reality or hallucinations during those high periods. Even though I was very wound up and hard to slow down, it never got to that point.

To clarify, have any of your hypomanic episodes, despite being brief, led to significant consequences or harm in your personal or professional life, such as legal issues, financial problems, or damaged relationships, that persisted even after the episode passed?

While we didn't have legal trouble or total financial ruin, those high periods definitely left some lasting strain. I got very snappy and irritable with my wife and kids when they tried to get me to slow down, and I neglected actual, paying orders because I was so distracted by my big ideas. That left us in a really tight spot financially once the high wore off.

Did any of your high episodes, despite not requiring hospitalization, lead to consequences that significantly impacted your life or relationships in a lasting way, beyond just the immediate period of being 'wired' or 'high'?

Even though I wasn't hospitalized, those high periods definitely caused lasting strain because I would get very snappy and defensive with my wife and kids when they tried to get me to slow down or questioned my unrealistic plans. On top of that, I was so caught up in big, restless ideas that I couldn't sit still to finish the actual orders I already had, which hurt my business reputation and contributed to the financial mess we are dealing with now.

Can you estimate the total duration of all your hypomanic episodes in the past year and compare it to the duration of your current depressive episode to help understand the pattern and severity of your mood swings?

In the past year, that high, wired phase right before my crash only lasted for a few weeks, whereas this deep, heavy depression has been going on steadily for about six months now. While these swings have been coming and going for several years, the low periods always last much longer and feel far more severe than those brief high-energy phases.

Have any of your hypomanic episodes, despite being brief, led to significant consequences or harm in your personal or professional life that persisted beyond the episode itself, such as damaged relationships or financial problems that you're still dealing with today?

Yes, that high period did cause lasting problems. I got very snappy and irritated with my family when they tried to warn me that my plans didn't make financial sense, and because I was so caught up in those grand ideas, I didn't finish the orders I already had. Falling behind on those invoices and missing delivery dates really hurt my business, and we are still dealing with the financial stress of it today.

Can you clarify if the total duration of your hypomanic episodes, although brief, when added together over the years, significantly impacts your overall functioning and relationships, compared to the duration and impact of your depressive episodes?

The depressive episodes are much longer, like this current six-month stretch, and they have a far more devastating, paralyzing impact on my daily life and work. The 'up' periods are just short bursts of energy, and while they did cause some strain with my wife when I got snappy, they never completely disabled me or pulled me away from life the way these heavy, endless lows do.

Can you confirm whether the duration and impact of your hypomanic episodes, although brief, have consistently been less severe and less impactful on your daily life compared to your depressive episodes, which seem to be longer and more debilitating?

Yes, that is exactly right. The high periods only last a few weeks and, despite some irritability and disorganization, they don't completely stop me from functioning. But these depressive phases, like this current six-month stretch, last so much longer and completely paralyze me, making it impossible to work, socialize, or do anything at all.

Have you ever experienced a hypomanic episode that, despite being brief, had a significant and lasting impact on your life, similar to the impact of your current depressive episode, in terms of causing substantial distress, impairment in social or occupational functioning, or necessitating intervention from others?

Yes, that 'up' period right before this crash actually had a major, lasting impact because I poured all my energy and money into those unrealistic plans to make the workshop a famous online brand, staying up until 3 AM and getting very snappy when my family tried to warn me. I was so distracted that I left actual client orders unfinished, which directly contributed to the business failing. That chaotic stretch is what set me up for this severe crash and the massive guilt I am carrying now.

Can you further describe how the impact of your hypomanic episodes, despite their brief duration, compares to the impact of your depressive episodes in terms of overall distress and impairment in your daily life and relationships?

While those high periods caused some strain—like getting snappy with my family and starting too many unfinished projects—the depressive episodes are far more devastating. During these lows, I completely shut down, stop working, pull away from my church and friends, and leave all the household responsibilities to my wife. The deep, heavy distress and those scary thoughts of death make the depressive phases much harder to handle.

Have your hypomanic episodes, although brief, ever reached a level of severity where they required intervention from others to prevent harm to yourself or others, or significantly impacted your social or occupational functioning in a lasting way?

No, those high periods never got so severe that I needed any kind of intervention to prevent harm or keep me safe. While I was definitely irritable and left a lot of projects unfinished, the real lasting damage and the struggle to keep up with my business and daily life have always happened during these heavy, depressed periods.

Can you clarify if the impact of your hypomanic episodes on your daily life and relationships has been consistently less severe than the impact of your depressive episodes, and if so, how you would rate the overall severity of your hypomanic episodes compared to your depressive episodes?

Yes, the high periods were definitely much less destructive; even though I was snappy and left projects unfinished, I still felt active and motivated. By contrast, these low periods are completely paralyzing, causing me to fall behind on work, withdraw from my wife and community, and even think about suicide. I would rate the depressive episodes as far more severe and harmful to my life.

Did any of your hypomanic episodes cause significant problems that led to major life changes or consequences, such as losing a job, ending a relationship, or experiencing financial ruin, which could indicate a difference in severity?

No, those up periods never led to anything catastrophic like divorce, bankruptcy, or losing my shop entirely, even though they caused some tension and left projects unfinished. The severe problems, like falling behind on invoices and completely withdrawing from life, really set in during this current low phase.
